label: Offset Shroud
iwEaNote: first component tagged EA-O -- Sec.2's own class, distinct from every IW-A/IW-P component classified so far. Not an attachment (no connector) and not a piping item (no section of its own); it is a roller-contact geometry modifier riding the pipe's own nodes.

artifactType.reason: Per the FBS/OAM reconciliation CSV (oam_part_assembly_status field): 'neither Part nor Assembly cleanly -- closer to an OAM geometric AssemblyFeature attached to the pipe artifact than an artifact itself. open -- new OAM subtype needed.' This is a stronger claim than a close call between the two existing values: the CSV argues the binary test itself is the wrong instrument for a component with no structural line of its own. candidate stays null (not 'Assembly') because the real candidate -- a third OAM category -- has no enum value to name yet; shared.oam.partAssemblyRule and the metaschema's artifactType.current/candidate enum would both need to grow a value before this can honestly read as either open-with-a-candidate or closed. current=Part is retained only because it is the least-wrong existing label and matches shared's live assignment, not because the classification question is settled.

note: OAM edge case: source docstring calls it 'neither Part nor Assembly cleanly -- closer to a geometric AssemblyFeature attached to the pipe artifact than an artifact itself' (per FBS/OAM reconciliation CSV). Recorded here as an openQuestion rather than overridden: this file follows shared's live Part assignment for consistency with the rest of the corpus, but the deeper OAM-conceptual mismatch (a component with no structural line of its own, riding another artifact's nodes) is not resolved by that assignment, only papered over by it.

edges.note: Func6 is a ProposedFunction, not yet in the authored edes:shared.nodes set -- see edges note on scope.functionGap
inverse-causality pair: GD-TP derives V from a free section (OD_comp); GD-SH takes V as the free input and the section stays untouched
contrast on taper contact normal: GD-TT's taper stays concentric (normal points at centreline); GD-SH's taper is an offset ramp (normal tilts away, genuine moment arises)

designCode.status: OPEN -- does not fit edes:shared.designCode rule
designCode.reason: shared.designCode's rule is keyed on section_at (pipe-shaped vs non-pipe interface). GD-SH.section_at is unconditionally None -- there is no cross-section for the rule to classify, because the component adds no material to the pipe (Sec.2.4). The rule's premise (a component realises Func1/Func3 via a real section) does not hold here at all.
designCode.consequence: no governing design code identified yet for a roller-contact geometry aid as a category -- open pending EDPR/EDIKB input, same open status as GD-VLV but for a different reason (GD-VLV has a section and a real code family, just not the shared one; GD-SH has no section to code-check)

scope.addsNoSection: Sec.2.4 -- adds no material to the pipe cross-section. section_at() is unconditionally None over the full domain, verified live (not just at centre_x).
scope.ownsNoStructuralLine: Sec.2.7 -- clamped to the pipe; rides the pipeline's own structural nodes. structural_nodes() and structural_lines() both return empty lists, verified live.
scope.vIsFree: the exact inverse of GD-TP/GD-TT: there V is DERIVED from a free section (OD_comp); here V is the FREE input and CL_lift is its consequence. Same symbol, opposite causality -- flagged explicitly in source docstring and in edges above.
scope.functionGap: no Function in edes:shared.nodes fits this component as originally authored (Func1/Func3 assume the component IS pipe-shaped and carries a section; Func2/Func4 assume a connector; Func5 assumes a literal piping item). Added edes:Func6 to shared.proposedFunctions to name the gap rather than force a realizes edge onto a Function that does not actually describe GD-SH's mechanism.
scope.continuousEvaluation: PREFERRED not MANDATORY node snapping (source docstring, geometry_nodes()) -- contact offset is evaluated CONTINUOUSLY at any x rather than tied to a discrete per-element section change, unlike GD-TP/GD-TT/GD-PIP/GD-VLV which all trigger a snapped mesh rebuild at their section steps.

free.name: V
free.meaning: DEPTH from the pipe centreline DOWN to the shroud's own contact surface. FREE here (contrast edes:GD-TP where the equivalent is derived).
free.note: depth below pipe C/L to the shroud's own deep-section contact surface (Sec.2.5). FREE here -- contrast GD-TP where the equivalent symbol V is derived.

free.name: L1
free.meaning: AXIAL LENGTH of the flat deep section, at constant V.

free.name: L2
free.meaning: AXIAL LENGTH of the taper ramp at EACH end. Total extent is L1 + 2*L2.
free.note: taper length each side. Corrected 16 Aug 2026 from 2.5*OD to 5*OD (see defects GD-SH-D1).

derived.name: CL_lift
derived.note: elevation above the baseline pipe-on-roller condition (Sec.2.6)

derived.name: halfExtent
derived.expr: halfExtent = L1/2 + L2  (flat deep section plus one taper ramp each side)
derived.meaning: HALF the component's axial footprint. extent = (centre_x - halfExtent, centre_x + halfExtent). Needed to place this component adjacent to another -- see edas:shared#/chaining.
derived.verifiedAt: the instance shown in verifiedWith below

params.defaultForNote: default_for(pipe) is the SINGLE place the 1D/10D/5D ratio is computed; dataclass literal defaults (V=0.4064, L1=4.064, L2=2.032) verified live to equal default_for(STD_PIPELINE) exactly -- callers building against a different pipe (incl. plot_schematic.py) should call default_for rather than recompute the ratio.

geometry.verifiedLive: geometry_nodes()=4 (tipL, deepL, deepR, tipR, all NodePriority.PREFERRED); structural_nodes()=[]; geometry_lines()=3 (taper/flat/taper), each with structural_line_id=PIPELINE_STRUCTURAL_LINE_ID and owns_contact=True; structural_lines()=[]
geometry.nodesOnOwnSurface: unlike GD-TP/GD-TT/GD-PIP whose nodes sit on the pipe centreline (y=0), GD-SH's 4 geometry nodes sit on the shroud's OWN surface (y = contact_at(x).y, verified nonzero at all 4 stations)
geometry.contact: owns full extent (all 3 segments), PIPE_ELEMENT load path, arm = abs(y) -- verified nonzero and equal to y at every probed x, confirming a genuine offset (not collinear with the axis) even on the flat section

sectionClaim.verified: section_at() returns None at every x, VERIFIED LIVE; contact_at() returns a real Contact (y=0.4064 at the default V) over the whole extent.
sectionClaim.consequence: THIS COMPONENT MAY OVERLAP ANY OTHER. Because it adds no material to the pipe cross-section it can nest over a thick pipe, a valve, or a chain of header segments without conflict -- which is exactly what ILS-SHTP does. Set ownership='lowest' when it overlaps another contact-owning component, because two components then claim the contact surface and the shroud is genuinely the deeper one, so nothing is being guessed.
sectionClaim.doNotGeneralise: Reading 'the shroud nests over a thick pipe, therefore components may nest' and applying it to a header segment is a REAL and OBSERVED error (5Sep26). A edes:GD-HdPipe running under a edes:GD-TP is two components both defining the pipe cross-section at one station -- a contradiction, not a nesting, and ownership='lowest' does not fix it because it arbitrates contact only. What nests is a component that claims NO section. See edas:shared#/sectionVersusContact.
sectionClaim.notInTheWeldChain: GD-SH is excluded from ils_builder.INLINE_CODES, so weld_chain() never welds it and unmated_gaps() ignores it. Its relation to the pipeline is a PositionOrientation against the centreline, not a Connection -- see edas:shared#/positionConstraints.

constraints.repair: increase V to at least the pipe radius
constraints.note: guards CL_lift>=0 -- below this the shroud would sit inside the pipe (source raise message states this explicitly)

nonConstraints: no upper bound on V/L1/L2 -- geometric validity != evidence coverage, same convention as GD-TP
no check relating L2 (taper length) to L1 (deep length) -- a taper longer than the deep section it flanks is not rejected
no check that provenance=DESIGN is inappropriate given the open designCode status

assemblyFeatures.status: not applicable -- GD-SH takes no connector by design (clamped to pipe, Sec.2.7). Contrast GD-TP, where the empty slots list is a real gap (Func2 needs one); here it correctly reflects the component's own definition.

behaviourDerived.mechanism: large OD/WT-equivalent stiffness-raising effect on the pipe beneath it (higher than GD-TP per source), PLUS a vertical offset to the pipeline that is usually the highest among IW-A/P/EA-O components -- two distinct effects (stiffness step is not owned by GD-SH itself since section_at is None; it is a consequence of the pipe element it clamps to. The offset IS owned by GD-SH.)
behaviourDerived.referenceBase: plain pipe at same stinger radius, same convention as GD-TP
behaviourDerived.tier: mechanism=ILS-tier; magnitude=SLAY-tier (unverified against EDIKB -- Phase 1 has not run, per shared.behaviourExpected)

rollerContact.default: yes -- entire reason for the component's existence (Sec.2's own stated purpose: to locally elevate the pipeline and control curvature)
rollerContact.continuousNotSnapped: contact evaluated continuously at any x, not tied to a discrete section-change node (see scope.continuousEvaluation)

usedInLayouts.note: Back-links to worked layouts containing this component, generated mechanically from the layout library on 1Sep26 -- not hand-written, so they cannot drift from it by authoring error, though they WILL go stale if the library changes and this is not regenerated. Their purpose is placement guidance: this file describes what the component IS and what its own constraints are, but says nothing about where along a header to put one or what to put either side of it. A worked archetype answers that by example. paramsUsed are the archetype's own values verbatim; anchors are published table rows that override them.

ILS-SH.purpose: Holds the pipeline off its natural catenary over a length, then ramps it back. Curvature concentrates at the catenary-side edge of the elevated zone -- a DIFFERENT mechanism from the two thick-body ar

ILS-SHTP.purpose: A thick body sitting INSIDE the shroud deep section. Both mechanisms act at once: the shroud lifts the pipe off its catenary (Type B1) while the thick body puts a stiffness step inside that elevated z

defects.summary: L2 (taper length each side) used the wrong multiplier: 2.5*OD (giving 1.016m) instead of the Sec.2.5-stated 5*OD (2.032m)
defects.fix: corrected in default_for() and the dataclass literal default together, per the 16 Aug 2026 source comment

regressionCase.status: none recorded yet -- GD-TP/GD-VLV both have a Foundation Sec.3 regression case; no equivalent has been run for GD-SH

openQuestions: Part vs Assembly artifact typing REMAINS OPEN for this component specifically, and is now the ONLY component where it is. The 1Sep26 project decision settled every other component (Part for GD-TP/GD-TT/GD-PIP/GD-VLV/GD-HdPipe/GD-BrPipe/GD-Con, Sub-Assembly for GD-ST/GD-SB/GD-B) and emptied shared.oam.partAssemblyRule's ArguableUnderThisTest list. GD-SH is untouched by that decision because its concern is different in kind: not 'which of the available values applies' but 'none of them does'. Its own source docstring argues for a third OAM category -- a geometric AssemblyFeature attached to the pipe artifact rather than an artifact in its own right -- which the Part/Assembly/Sub-Assembly enum still cannot express. Adding Sub-Assembly did not help here: GD-SH's problem is having no structural line of its own at all, not being subordinate to something.
no Function in the current authored set (Func1-5) fits GD-SH's mechanism -- Func6 added to shared.proposedFunctions as a placeholder pending a real decision on whether to add it to the authored set
iwEaClass enum in EDES_METASCHEMA.json only lists IW-A/IW-P -- EA-O needed for this file and does not yet validate against the current metaschema (see metaschema change accompanying this file)

no relationship checked between GD-SH and a co-located GD-TP/GD-TT/GD-PIP/GD-VLV occupying the same pipeline stretch -- Assembly.section_at/contact_at ownership arbitration between a section-owning component and a contact-only component sharing one span is untested
designCode left fully open (see designCode.consequence) -- no category has been proposed even provisionally, unlike GD-VLV which at least names API 6D/ASME B16.34 as the likely family

inputsRequired.readAlso: edes:shared -- REQUIRED, not optional. V is the FREE input here, the opposite causality to edes:GD-TP where the equivalent quantity is derived. Do not compute V from a target OD; it IS the input.

headerPipeline.OD_pipe: REQUIRED, metres -- the HEADER pipeline outside diameter
headerPipeline.why: No default exists for either. This component's parameters, defaults and constraints are evaluated against the pipe it is built on; without both, none of them can be resolved.

componentParams.required: none beyond placement -- every free parameter has a usable default

optional.V: defaults to 1.0*OD_pipe. m. depth below pipe C/L to the shroud's own deep-section contact surface (Sec.2.5). FREE here -- contrast GD-TP where the equivalent symbol V is derived
optional.L1: defaults to 10.0*OD_pipe. m. deep-section length, flat, constant V
optional.L2: defaults to 5.0*OD_pipe. m. taper length each side. Corrected 16 Aug 2026 from 2.5*OD to 5*OD (see defects GD-SH-D1)

placement.centre_x: REQUIRED to place the component. EDES gives NO guidance on the value. See usedInLayouts for worked precedents (ILS-SH, ILS-SHTP), or query.

inputsRequired.ifMissing: Anything listed as required, having no default, and not supplied by the person must be QUERIED. Do not assume a value and do not carry one over from a worked example -- a precedent shows what was once chosen, not what this case needs.

assemblyRef: edas:shared -- assembly-level knowledge this file deliberately does not carry: build sequence, id convention, the chaining equation, ownership arbitration, section-vs-contact, association format and the emit format.
